content.text:
h02.

**Delivery function — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`**
The outbound delivery executes in `Post()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`), specifically at the `safeClient.Do(req)` call on line 152. This is where the actual outbound HTTP POST to the external endpoint is sent. (Notifications are enqueued via `PostAsync` and drained by worker goroutines started in `init()`, but the request itself fires in `Post`.)

**Protection mechanism — `internal/webhook/webhook.go` (+ `internal/webhook/validate.go`)**
The primary, delivery-time protection is `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:59`), wired into the shared `safeClient`'s `http.Transport.DialContext` (lines 32–37). At dial time it resolves the target host and rejects any resolved address that falls in a reserved/private range via `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:44`), which checks against `reservedCIDRs` (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/cloud IMDS `169.254.169.254`, and IPv6 equivalents — `internal/webhook/validate.go:14`). Because the check happens at connection time on the actually-resolved IP, it also defeats DNS-rebinding.

There is also an up-front check, `ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`), which enforces http/https scheme and blocks reserved IPs when a webhook URL is configured. Note both guards can be disabled by the `AllowPrivateIPs` flag (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`) for self-hosted local-network use.
